title: Cancellation in Async Rust
goal: Dropping a future cancels execution at the current await point.

sections.text: In Rust, dropping a future immediately cancels it. If a future is waiting at an `.await` point and gets dropped, execution stops right there.

sections.caption: Dropping a future discards its internal state machine.

sections.text: When a future is dropped, all local variables currently stored inside its state machine are dropped as well. No cleanup code after the `.await` will ever run.

This makes cancellation fast and clean, but it requires care. If an `async fn` holds partial state in local variables across an `.await`, that state is lost when cancelled. Keep persistent state in struct fields outside the `async fn`.

explanation: Dropping a future cancels execution at the current await point.
